demo_id_note: An internal demonstration identifier. It is NOT an NHS ODS code and does not identify any real organisation.
product_title: Midshire University Hospitals Trust Control Tower
status_line: Adult ED planning demonstrator · simulated data, not a live patient feed.
disclaimers: Midshire University Hospitals Trust is a fictional demonstration identity. It is not a real South East trust.
Every figure on screen is a simulation output or a labelled input assumption. Nothing here is a live patient feed or a connected digital twin.
Rota and cost inputs are illustrative. Staffing outputs are aggregate planning rotas, not a clinically approved or safe-staffing roster.
The adult-only, SDEC-extended build has NOT inherited the source model's validation. Treat results as directional.

foundation.summary: Cambridge-derived. The adult pathway, routing, service times, physical capacity, hospital bed model and demand shape are taken from the Cambridge University Hospitals (RGT) build of this tool, then changed: the paediatric cohort is removed, SDEC is reachable from streaming and RAT, a decision-to-admit milestone is added, and the rota, costs and SDEC size are illustrative. The front-facing name is fictional; the technical provenance is not anonymised by renaming.
foundation.validation_status: The Cambridge build was validated per area against CUH's own data (see docs/CUH_DATA_LOG.md). This Midshire build changes the cohort, pathway and staffing, so that validation does not carry over. Its own conformance checks (python3 -m uec_hybrid.midshire.validate) confirm the pathway behaves as specified; nothing confirms it matches a real hospital.

cohort.name: adult
cohort.label: Adults only (the paediatric ED cohort is excluded)

paediatric_share_excluded.provenance: Share of the source trust's front-door attendances seen in its paediatric ED area, Feb-Jul 2026 (rgt_published.json paediatric_share). The published age-based share is higher (19.7%); the area-based share is used because the model routes by area.

adult_attendances_per_day.provenance: 400.5 x (1 - 0.1335) = 347.0 adult attendances a day. Children are REMOVED from demand, not re-routed into adult areas.

assumptions: The adult hour-of-arrival shape is the source trust's all-ages front-door shape (no adult-only hourly split exists).
The ambulance share (19.1%) is the all-ages share applied to adults; the adult share is probably higher because children are conveyed less often.
The mental-health share (2.6%) is the all-ages Type 1 and 2 share applied to adults.
The acuity mix is the source trust's ADULT area mix (resus / majors trolleys / majors ambulant / minors), so it needs no adjustment.

provenance.rat: Source trust: 24/7, ambulance arrivals assessed on arrival.
provenance.utc: Source trust: 08:00-00:00 envelope. Overnight, minors divert to the 24/7 ambulatory area (a labelled source-trust assumption).
provenance.sdec: ILLUSTRATIVE for Midshire: 08:00-22:00, ED-streamed patients only.
provenance.frailty: Source trust template: 08:00-18:00 (hours still unconfirmed at source).

excluded.paeds: Adult demonstrator: paediatric area removed with its demand, staff and capacity.
excluded.eemac: Not in operation at the source trust.
excluded.cdu: Not in operation at the source trust.
excluded.mh: No dedicated mental-health area at the source trust; mental-health patients follow the mental-health admission sub-route.

provenance.cubicle: Source trust ops return: 34 majors cubicles/trolley spaces.
provenance.resus_bay: Source trust ops return: 6 resus bays.
provenance.fit_to_sit_chair: Source trust ops return: 8 chairs + 9 ambulatory rooms.
provenance.utc_room: Source trust ops return: 15 UTC rooms.
provenance.sdec_chair: ILLUSTRATIVE for Midshire: 12 ED-facing SDEC chairs (the source trust's 60 also serve GP and other referral streams, which this demonstrator deliberately does not add).
provenance.handover_bay: Source trust ops return: 3 ambulance handover bays.
provenance.ct_scanner: Source trust ops return: 3 CT scanners (shared with inpatients).
provenance.xray_room: Source trust ops return: 3 plain X-ray rooms.
provenance.fau_bed: Template estimate (12 at 320/day, scaled to the source trust's size = 15). Not a real count.
provenance.minor_injury_space: Source trust: 0 - minors are seen in the UTC (removes the ED minor-injury node).

space_staffing.note: ILLUSTRATIVE, editable planning ratios - NOT clinical safe-staffing standards. A space only opens if staff on shift cover it (open = min(physical spaces, staff x spaces per staff)). The 1 nurse : 4 cubicles ratio is the source model's template value; the other three are Midshire illustrations. Fit-to-sit chairs, handover bays, CT and X-ray have no staffing ratio in the model (stated, not hidden).

downstream.provenance: The source trust's whole-hospital bed model as the engine resolves it (KH03 beds 1,068 and occupancy 89.26%; flows are template rates scaled to the source trust's size). The ED cohort changes, the hospital does not.
downstream.community_note: Community / virtual-ward capacity is set to NONE. The source trust reports 1 virtual-ward place a day, mostly step-down after discharge, so ED-facing capacity is effectively nil. The source model's community-pull mechanism (a signal held for an hour at a time) cannot represent a single daily place without diverting about ten patients a day, so Midshire models no community route rather than represent it wrongly.
downstream.aggregate_assumption: Wards are one aggregate bed stock. Discharges per hour scale with how full the stock is, and occupancy lengthens the wait for a bed through a smooth multiplier. The model does not allocate patients to specific wards or model transfer constraints.

sdec.name: Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC)
sdec.routing_note: ILLUSTRATIVE eligibility assumptions (no source-trust figure exists for the ED-streamed share). From streaming: 10% of acuity-2 and 15% of acuity-3 walk-ins go straight to SDEC. 15% of acuity-2 walk-ins are referred to RAT for senior assessment, and RAT sends 10% of acuity-2 and 15% of acuity-3 patients (ambulance or walk-in) to SDEC. Everyone else follows the source routing.
sdec.max_wait_note: ILLUSTRATIVE: a patient who has waited 90 minutes without an SDEC chair and clinician - including anyone still queued when SDEC staff go off shift - is redirected to the ED area for their acuity, rather than waiting overnight for a unit that has closed.
sdec.closed_note: When SDEC is closed, a patient who would have gone there is redirected to the ED area for their acuity (the same area they would have used without SDEC). Patients already in SDEC at closing time finish their care. Nobody is removed or discharged by the closure.
sdec.service_note: ILLUSTRATIVE split of the SDEC stay: a 45-minute clinician assessment (holds an SDEC doctor) then tests, treatment and observation in the chair (no clinician held). The care time (mean 160 minutes) was CALIBRATED so the modelled time in SDEC matches the source trust's SDEC median time in department: 247 minutes modelled (4 replications) against 247 observed, June 2026; 46% within four hours of entering SDEC against 49% observed (Feb-Jul 2026).
sdec.selection_caveat: The model picks SDEC patients at random within acuity 2 and 3; it cannot pick the clinically suitable ones. Those patients then skip the ED imaging and results-and-decision steps of their acuity's pathway and are admitted at SDEC's 16.1% rate. In the baseline, SDEC streaming adds about 8 points to the four-hour measure. Treat any SDEC-driven improvement as an UPPER BOUND.
sdec.admission_provenance: Source trust SDEC admission rate, Feb-Jul 2026 (4,179 of 26,022).
sdec.reporting_note: SDEC time counts INSIDE the ED attendance: the four-hour clock does not stop at transfer to SDEC, and SDEC patients stay in every denominator. Transfer to SDEC is neither a discharge nor an admission.

mental_health.provenance: Source trust mental-health disposals, 1 May - 12 Aug 2026: 195 admitted of 1,067 (rgt_published.json cuh_extracts.mental_health). Replaces the source build's fallback, which admitted every mental-health patient because there is no MH area.
mental_health.not_modelled: Did-not-wait (12.2%) and left-without-treatment (14.0%) rates for mental-health patients are recorded at source but not modelled.

rota.convention: Whole hours 0-24. A shift whose end is at or before its start runs past midnight and belongs to the day it starts. 'Mon-Sun' rows repeat every day; other day patterns apply only on those days.
rota.provenance: ILLUSTRATIVE. Built from the Model ED template rota as the source build resolves it (scaled to the source trust's 400.5/day), with paediatric doctors removed, ENPs replaced by UTC practitioners, and resus, UTC and SDEC staffing added so the space-staffing ratios open the physical spaces. Not any trust's real roster.

cost_table.status: ILLUSTRATIVE Midshire demonstration rates. They are not current NHS Agenda for Change or medical pay rates, nor any trust's rates.
cost_table.inclusions: Effective hourly cost = basic rate x (1 + employer on-cost %) x (1 + average unsocial-hours enhancement %), blended with the bank/agency share at its all-in rate. A FULLY LOADED rate, if entered, is used as given and nothing is added to it - it must already include on-costs, enhancements and any agency mix.

estates.status: ILLUSTRATIVE unit costs for demonstration. A blank cost is shown as 'not costed', never as £0, and a package containing one is never ranked as fully costed.

annualisation.note: For ranking only: annualised comparison cost = recurring annual cost + one-off capital / 15 years (straight line, no discounting, no residual value). Capital and recurring costs are always shown separately as well.

ct_scanner.label: CT scanner
ct_scanner.staffing_not_modelled: Radiographer staffing is not modelled; a new scanner is assumed staffed whenever open.

inpatient_beds.label: New inpatient beds
inpatient_beds.note: NEW physical beds. Recurring cost per bed per year is an illustrative all-in ward cost (including ward staffing, which is not in the ED rota). Capital not costed. Different from freeing existing beds.

ward_discharge_pct.label: Faster ward discharge (frees EXISTING beds)
ward_discharge_pct.note: An improvement in the rate wards discharge patients. Not a new bed. Not costed: it depends on what would deliver it.

community_capacity.label: Community / virtual-ward places
community_capacity.note: Illustrative recurring cost per place per year.

target.label: 90% of adult patients leave the emergency department within 4 hours
target.note: The share of adult patients who leave the emergency department (admitted, transferred or discharged) within the chosen time, counted from arrival. 90% within 4 hours is a planning target you can change; it is not a statement of the current national standard.

engine.note: Each replication simulates a 1-day warm-up, 6 observed days and a 12-hour drain. The cohort is everyone arriving in the 6 observed days; the drain lets them finish. Baseline and every scenario use the SAME seeds (matched comparisons). Shortlisted packages are re-run on a SEPARATE validation seed set, so selection is not mistaken for confirmation.

levers.title: +4 majors cubicles (with any nurses needed to open them)
+1 resus bay (with any resus nurses needed)
+3 UTC rooms (with any UTC practitioners needed)
+4 SDEC chairs (with any SDEC nurses needed)
SDEC open until midnight (with matching SDEC staff)

search.note: The search only tests the changes listed here, at these sizes, and combinations of them built step by step (see the method on screen). It cannot change clinical durations, routing probabilities or demand. It does not prove that a target is impossible in the real hospital or that the package found is the cheapest possible.

lever_text.note: Plain-language names and descriptions of the changes the package search can test (display text only; the search uses the levers above).

nurse_day.name: Extra majors nurse by day
nurse_day.change: Add one Band 5 nurse in majors, 08:00 to 20:00, every day.
nurse_day.why: Majors cubicles only open when there is a nurse to staff them.
nurse_day.look_for: Shorter waits for a majors cubicle during the day.

nurse_night.name: Extra majors nurse overnight
nurse_night.change: Add one Band 5 nurse in majors, 20:00 to 08:00, every night.
nurse_night.why: Night staffing often decides how many cubicles stay open.

sho_late.name: Extra junior doctor into the evening
sho_late.change: Add one ED junior doctor, 14:00 to 02:00, every day.
sho_late.why: Doctors are busiest from mid-afternoon into the night.
sho_late.look_for: Patients seen sooner in the afternoon and evening.

reg_night.name: Extra registrar overnight
reg_night.change: Add one ED registrar, 22:00 to 08:00, every night.
reg_night.why: With fewer senior doctors overnight, decisions take longer.
reg_night.look_for: Shorter waits overnight and fewer 12-hour stays.

cons_eve.name: Extra consultant into the evening
cons_eve.change: Add one ED consultant, 14:00 to midnight, every day.
cons_eve.why: In the evening peak, patients often wait for a senior review.
cons_eve.look_for: Faster decisions in the evening peak.

rat_day.name: Strengthen RAT during peak hours
rat_day.change: Add one senior RAT clinician, 10:00 to 22:00, every day.
rat_day.why: Ambulance patients and some walk-ins see RAT first, so a busy RAT holds up everything behind it.
rat_day.look_for: Shorter waits for RAT and better 4-hour performance.

stream_day.name: Extra streaming nurse by day
stream_day.change: Add one streaming nurse at the front door, 08:00 to 20:00, every day.
stream_day.why: Walk-in patients wait at the front door until they are streamed.

utc_prac.name: Extra UTC practitioner, afternoon to midnight
utc_prac.change: Add one UTC practitioner, 12:00 to midnight, every day.
utc_prac.why: Minor illness and injury queues build in the afternoon and evening.

sdec_doc.name: Extra SDEC doctor on weekdays
sdec_doc.change: Add one SDEC doctor, 10:00 to 20:00, Monday to Friday.
sdec_doc.why: SDEC can only take patients when there is a doctor to see them.
sdec_doc.look_for: More patients treated in SDEC instead of waiting in majors.

porter.name: Extra porter by day
porter.change: Add one porter, 08:00 to 20:00, every day.
porter.why: Admitted patients wait for a porter before they move to the ward.
porter.look_for: Shorter waits for transfer to the ward.

cubicles_4.name: Four more majors cubicles
cubicles_4.change: Add four majors cubicles, with the nurses needed to open them.
cubicles_4.why: Majors patients wait when every cubicle is full.
cubicles_4.look_for: Shorter waits for a majors cubicle.

resus_1.name: One more resus bay
resus_1.change: Add one resus bay, with the resus nurses needed to staff it.
resus_1.why: The sickest patients need a resus bay straight away.

utc_rooms_3.name: Three more UTC rooms
utc_rooms_3.change: Add three UTC rooms, with the UTC practitioners needed to open them.
utc_rooms_3.why: UTC queues build when every room is in use.

f2s_4.name: Four more fit-to-sit spaces
f2s_4.change: Add four fit-to-sit spaces for majors patients who are well enough to sit.
f2s_4.why: These patients wait when the fit-to-sit area is full.
f2s_4.look_for: Shorter waits for majors patients who can sit.

sdec_chairs_4.name: Four more SDEC chairs
sdec_chairs_4.change: Add four SDEC chairs, with the SDEC nurses needed to staff them.
sdec_chairs_4.why: SDEC turns patients away when every chair is in use.

sdec_late.name: Keep SDEC open until midnight
sdec_late.change: Open SDEC from 08:00 to midnight instead of 22:00, with a doctor and three nurses for the extra hours.
sdec_late.why: Patients who arrive after SDEC closes are treated in the main ED instead.
sdec_late.look_for: More patients through SDEC in the late evening.

ct_1.name: One more CT scanner
ct_1.why: Patients waiting for a CT scan can't get a decision until the scan is done.
ct_1.look_for: Shorter waits for CT and for results.

beds_20.name: Twenty more inpatient beds
beds_20.change: Open 20 more inpatient beds in the hospital.
beds_20.why: Admitted patients wait in ED until a ward bed is free.
beds_20.look_for: Shorter waits for a bed and fewer 12-hour stays.

discharge_10.name: Faster ward discharges
discharge_10.change: Wards discharge patients 10% faster, so beds free up sooner.
discharge_10.why: Admitted ED patients are waiting for the beds that ward discharges free up.

groups.label: Waiting for first assessment
groups.description: Arrived and waiting to be streamed (walk-ins) or for an ambulance handover bay (ambulance arrivals).

groups.label: Initial assessment and handover
groups.description: Streaming, the ambulance handover itself, and rapid assessment and treatment (RAT) by a senior clinician.

groups.label: Clinical assessment and treatment
groups.description: The adult treatment areas, SDEC, the frailty unit, and waiting for results or a decision after diagnostics.

states.label: Waiting for a majors cubicle or clinician

groups.label: Diagnostics
groups.description: Imaging the model represents: CT and plain X-ray. Patients return to the results-and-decision step afterwards.

groups.label: Next destination / leaving ED
groups.description: After the decision: waiting for an inpatient bed, transfer to the ward, discharge preparation, and onward referral.

flow_map.note: The boxes on the Patient flow maps. Each unit is one or more occupancy states (stable node id and phase) or a decision milestone, and every state belongs to exactly one unit. Steps that are not units (diagnostics decision, disposition, SDEC outcome, SDEC-closed redirect) are instantaneous routing points: patients pass through them and the map links the steps on either side. col/row place a unit inside its group's detail map.
